This report presents the results of a Gap Assessment conducted by AETHERIS 
TECHNOLOGIES PVT LTD on IP addresses as per the project scope. 
 
Purpose of Assessment: 
• Identify Infrastructure GAP: Test the IPs to detect technical gap and evaluate 
whether these flaws could be exploited by a malicious user to compromise 
security. 
• Provide Risk Mitigation Recommendations: Offer guidance on mitigating risks 
that may arise if these gaps are successfully exploited. 
 
The following sections detail the identified Gaps, their severity, and the results of the 
Gap Assessment for the IPs. The detailed technical findings section includes identified 
gap and recommendations for mitigating the associated security risks. The assessment 
was conducted according to standard Gap methodologies. 
 
 
During the assessment, the testing team considered the latest Gap and security threats. 
The opinions provided in this report are valid for the period during which the assessment 
was performed and are based on the information available at that time. Any projections 
or conclusions drawn from these findings may be affected by changes made to the 
network, application, or system in the future. Please note that the findings reflect the 
conditions observed during the assessment and may not necessarily represent the current 
state. 
1. INTRODUCTION
sections.8:
8 
 
 
 
• Unsupported Windows OS (Remote) 
Observation: The system is running an unsupported version of Windows OS. 
• Microsoft RDP RCE (CVE-2019-0708) (BlueKeep) (uncredentialed check) 
Observation: The system is vulnerable to BlueKeep (CVE-2019-0708), a serious 
flaw in Microsoft Remote Desktop (RDP). An attacker can exploit this weakness 
without login credentials to gain control of the system. This may lead to 
unauthorized access, malware infection, or system compromise. 
 
• MS11-030: Vulnerability in DNS Resolution Could Allow 
Remote Code Execution (2509553) (remote check) 
Observation: The system is vulnerable to MS11-030 due to improper 
handling of DNS resolution, allowing potential remote code execution. 
This critical flaw can be exploited remotely, compromising system integrity 
without user interaction. 
• OpenSSL 1.0.1 < 1.0.1q Multiple Vulnerabilities 
Observation: The system is running an outdated version of OpenSSL (below 
1.0.1q) that contains multiple known security vulnerabilities. These 
weaknesses can be exploited by attackers to intercept encrypted 
communications or disrupt services, increasing the risk of data exposure and 
system compromise. 
 
• SSL Medium Strength Cipher Suites Supported (SWEET32) 
Observation: The system supports SSL medium-strength cipher suites 
that are vulnerable to the SWEET32 attack. This weakness may allow 
an attacker to decrypt parts of encrypted communication over time, 
putting sensitive data at risk. 
 
• SNMP Agent Default Community Name (public) 
Observation: The SNMP service is using the default community name 
“public”, which is widely known. An attacker can use this to access 
system information without authorization, potentially leading to 
information disclosure or further attacks. 
• IP Forwarding Enabled 
Observation: IP forwarding is enabled on the system, allowing it to route 
network traffic between different networks. If not required, this can be misused 
by attackers to redirect or monitor traffic, increasing the risk of unauthorized 
network access. 
4. OBSERVATION
sections.9:
9 
 
 
 
• Unsupported Windows OS (remote): Lack of security updates makes the system 
vulnerable to exploitation, leading to potential breaches. 
 
• Microsoft RDP RCE (CVE-2019-0708) (BlueKeep) (uncredentialed check): The 
presence of the Microsoft RDP BlueKeep vulnerability (CVE-2019-0708) allows an 
attacker to remotely execute code on the affected system without authentication. 
Successful exploitation can lead to complete system takeover, installation of malware, 
ransomware spread, or use of the system as a launch point for further attacks within the 
network. 
 
• 
MS11-030: Vulnerability in DNS Resolution Could Allow Remote Code Execution 
(2509553) (remote check): The MS11-030 DNS resolution vulnerability can be 
exploited remotely to execute malicious code by sending specially crafted DNS 
responses. This may result in system compromise, service disruption, or unauthorized 
access to internal resources, affecting overall network stability and security. 
• 
OpenSSL 1.0.1 < 1.0.1q Multiple Vulnerabilities: Use of outdated OpenSSL 
versions (below 1.0.1q) exposes the system to multiple cryptographic vulnerabilities. 
Attackers may exploit these weaknesses to intercept encrypted communications, 
manipulate data in transit, or cause denial-of-service conditions, leading to potential 
data leakage. 
• SSL Medium Strength Cipher Suites Supported (SWEET32): Support for SSL 
medium-strength cipher suites vulnerable to SWEET32 weakens encrypted 
communications. Long-lived or repeated sessions may allow attackers to decrypt 
sensitive information, increasing the risk of credential theft and data exposure. 
 
• SNMP Agent Default Community Name (public): The SNMP default 
community name “public” allows unauthorized users to query system and network 
information. This information can be leveraged for reconnaissance, helping attackers 
identify targets, configurations, and weaknesses for further exploitation. 
 
• IP Forwarding Enabled: With IP forwarding enabled, the system can route traffic 
between networks, which may be abused to intercept, redirect, or monitor network 
communications. If compromised, the host could be used for man-in-the-middle attacks 
or lateral movement within the network. 
5. IMPACT

check) 
 
Risk

172.16.10.11, 172.16.1.100, 172.16.2.175 
Description 
Microsoft RDP RCE (CVE-2019-0708), commonly known as BlueKeep, 
is a critical vulnerability in the Remote Desktop Services of certain 
Windows systems. It allows an attacker to execute arbitrary code on the 
target system without authentication by sending specially crafted RDP 
requests, potentially leading to complete system compromise. 
Mitigation 
• Apply the official Microsoft security patch for CVE-2019-0708 on all 
affected systems immediately. 
• Disable Remote Desktop Services (RDP) if it is not required. 
• Enable Network Level Authentication (NLA) for RDP. 
• Restrict RDP access using firewalls or VPNs and allow only trusted 
IP addresses. 
• Regularly update and patch Windows systems to prevent exploitation 
of known vulnerabilities. 
 
 
➢ MS11-030: Vulnerability in DNS Resolution Could Allow Remote Code 
Execution (2509553) (remote check): 
 
Risk 
CRITICAL 
IP address 
172.16.0.120, 172.16.1.228, 172.16.0.42, 172.16.2.80, 172.16.2.164, 
172.16.1.100, 172.16.0.20, 172.16.1.255, 172.16.2.175 
Description 
MS11-030 is a bug in Windows that can let hackers run harmful code on 
your computer by sending fake DNS responses. It can happen without any 
user action and may give the attacker full control. 
Mitigation 
• Apply the official Microsoft patch (KB2509553) immediately from the 
MS11-030 security bulletin. 
• Ensure systems are running supported and fully updated versions of 
Windows. 
• Restrict outbound DNS traffic to trusted internal DNS servers using 
firewall rules. 
• Monitor DNS traffic for anomalies and use intrusion 
detection/prevention systems (IDS/IPS).

➢ OpenSSL 1.0.1 < 1.0.1q Multiple Vulnerabilities 
 
Risk 
HIGH 
IP address 
172.16.10.5, 172.16.3.195, 172.16.8.235 
Description 
OpenSSL versions 1.0.1 earlier than 1.0.1q contain multiple known 
security vulnerabilities that affect how encrypted communications are 
handled. These weaknesses may allow attackers to decrypt sensitive data, 
perform man-in-the-middle attacks, or cause service disruption, putting the 
confidentiality and integrity of data at risk. 
Mitigation 
• Upgrade OpenSSL to version 1.0.1q or later (or a currently 
supported stable version). 
• Apply the latest security patches provided by the operating system 
or application vendor. 
• Restart affected services after upgrading OpenSSL to ensure the 
fixes take effect. 
• Disable weak or deprecated SSL/TLS protocols and cipher suites. 
• Regularly monitor and update cryptographic libraries to address 
newly discovered vulnerabilities.

Description 
The system supports SSL/TLS medium-strength cipher suites that are 
vulnerable to the SWEET32 attack. This attack targets 64-bit block ciphers 
(like 3DES) and can allow an attacker to gradually decrypt sensitive data from 
encrypted sessions, potentially exposing passwords, cookies, or other 
confidential information. 
Mitigation 
• Disable all 64-bit block ciphers (e.g., 3DES) in SSL/TLS 
configurations. 
• Configure servers to use strong, modern cipher suites such as AES- 
GCM or ChaCha20. 
• Apply the latest updates and patches to SSL/TLS libraries and 
applications. 
• Test SSL/TLS configuration using tools like Qualys SSL Labs to 
ensure weak ciphers are removed. 
• Regularly review and update encryption policies to follow current 
best practices.

Description 
The SNMP service on the system is using the default community name 
“public,” which is widely known. This allows anyone with network access to 
query the SNMP agent and gather sensitive information about the system, 
such as device configuration, running services, and network details. 
Exploiting this can help attackers plan further attacks. 
Mitigation 
• Change the SNMP community name from the default 
“public” to a strong, unique string. 
• Limit SNMP access to trusted IP addresses only. 
• Disable SNMP on devices or systems where it is not 
required. 
• Use SNMPv3 instead of SNMPv1/v2, as it provides 
authentication and encryption. 
• Regularly audit SNMP configurations to ensure secure 
settings are maintained.
